title: Safety Data Sheets: four different locations, several missing
whatWeFound: The handbook says SDS binders are on the shared Google Drive. The spill procedure says the WhatsApp group or Drive. The Safety Plan says the supply kit. The daily task list says a binder in the vehicle. All-Purpose Cleaner and All-Purpose Cleaning Vinegar (Lavender) have no SDS, and the Dawn SDS link looks broken.
nextStep: Pick one primary location plus one on-site copy, state it in every document, and get the missing sheets.

title: Job timer: start at home or at the client's door?
whatWeFound: The Employee Handbook (3.5, 5.2, 10B) says to start the job timer when you leave home for your first job, and that travel between jobs is paid. The Clock-In and Job Documentation SOP says to start the timer when you begin work at the client's home.
nextStep: Pick one rule. Have your attorney or CPA confirm the compliant rule, then update both documents and tell the team in writing.

title: Bleach: handbook prohibits it, Toilet Brush Protocol uses it
whatWeFound: Handbook 9.3 says use of bleach is strictly prohibited. The Toilet Brush Protocol tells specialists to use a Clorox toilet wand and pod. The Clorox wand and pods are not on the inventory or SDS list.
nextStep: Decide whether the Clorox pod is allowed. Change the handbook or the protocol to match, add the product and its SDS to the inventory, and tell the team.

title: Pay schedule: every two weeks or the 1st and 15th?
whatWeFound: The handbook says paychecks are bi-weekly. The Operations Tracker says to process payroll on the 1st and 15th.
nextStep: Confirm what payroll actually runs. Fix whichever document is wrong.

title: Final paycheck and equipment deadlines differ from the handbook
whatWeFound: The Offboarding Checklist says final paycheck and equipment within 48 hours. The handbook gives different deadlines depending on how the employment ended.
nextStep: Use the handbook deadlines until your attorney says otherwise, and rewrite the checklist to match.

title: Three-month raise wording is both promised and discretionary
whatWeFound: Handbook 3.1 says employees meeting expectations receive a $1.00 hourly raise at three months, while also stating all raises are discretionary.
nextStep: Confirm the intended rule and approve consistent wording.

title: Maintenance leave-behind conflicts with recurring scope and add-ons
whatWeFound: Maintenance leave-behind lists grout scrubbing, inside medicine cabinet and under couch cushions. Recurring SOP excludes grout/inside cabinets; Add-On SOP labels upholstery vacuuming as add-ons.
nextStep: Confirm recurring inclusions and exclusions, then align the leave-behind and SOPs.

title: Changed-price script does not request the confirmation required by SOP

nextStep: Revise the script to ask for explicit approval.

title: Extra-time charge vs. "never charge above the quoted range"
whatWeFound: Scopes say $25 per 30 minutes may apply when a job runs over. The New Cleaning Request SOP says never charge above what the customer was told.
nextStep: State which rule wins for phone-quoted first cleans, and when the $25 charge applies.

title: Service area: Beaverton in some documents only
whatWeFound: Two SOPs list Beaverton as a service area. The phone script, VA course, Deluxe scope and Difference page list eight cities and not Beaverton.
nextStep: Confirm the service area and make every document list the same cities.

title: Quoting: range plus deposit, or one price over the phone?
whatWeFound: The New Cleaning Request SOP quotes a range and takes a deposit with an optional walk-through. The VA course says to state one price and close over the phone with no walk-through.
nextStep: Decide which method is current and rewrite the others.

title: Three owner decisions still open inside the VA Sales course

title: 18 recurring tasks were assigned to Megan, who is no longer with the company
